<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:transfer}
Suppose that $k>\max\{1,N/2\}$ and $\sup_{t<T_{\max}}\|G(t)\|_{L^k}\le C_G$. Then both components $u$ and $v$ have upper bounds for any finite time, which means that the solution $(u,v)$ is global.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Under the assumptions of (\ref{zijia1}), $\delta_1(x), \delta_2(x)\geq 0$, $u_0(x), v_0(x)>0$ for every $x\in \Omega$, and $\frac{\partial u_0}{\partial \nu}=\frac{\partial v_0}{\partial \nu}=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, there exists a unique global positive classical solution to (\ref{eq:pde}).
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:floor}
If at least one of $\delta_1(x)$ and $\delta_2(x)$ is nontrivial, then there is a constant $\eta_v>0$ such that $v(x,t)\ge\eta_v$ for all $x\in \bar{\Omega}$ and $t<T_{\max}$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:source}
Assume that at least one of $\delta_1(x)$ and $\delta_2(x)$ is nontrivial. Choose
\begin{equation}\label{eq:closed-weights}
m>M,\qquad 0<n\le cm,\qquad mnK\le(m-1)(n+1).
\end{equation}
If $a_1>H(\frac{n}{m})$, the solution is global and uniformly bounded. Especially, if $\delta_1\equiv 0$ and $\delta_2\not\equiv0$, the sufficient condition can be relaxed as $a_1\ge H(\frac{n}{m})$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:tc}
Assume that $\delta_1(x)=\delta_2(x)\equiv 0$ for every $x\in \Omega$, (\ref{zijia1}) holds and the positive initial datum $u_0$ and $v_0$ which satisfy compatible condition $\frac{\partial u_0}{\partial \nu}=\frac{\partial v_0}{\partial \nu}=0$. If $\mu=a_1-a_2c-\Phi_{\theta}(\frac{n}{m})\geq 0$, then the solution to (\ref{eq:pde}) is boundedness.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:companion}
Let $\delta_1=\delta_2\equiv0$. Take $m>M$ and $n=cm$. If $mnK\le(m-1)(n+1)$ and
$$
L=\frac{m(s+1)}{r}-n=\frac{mq}{p(p-1)}\ge 1, 
$$
then the solution is global and uniformly bounded if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:companion-damping}
a_1>H(\min\{c,y_*\}),\qquad y_*=\theta a_2^{\theta-1}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, there exist $\xi,\omega>0$, depending only on the chosen $m,n$ and fixed coefficients in equations, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comp-decay}
F_{\xi}(t):=E(t)+\xi\int_{\Omega} v^L(x,t)dx
\le F_{\xi}(0)e^{-\omega t}
\end{equation}
and
 $$\|G(t)\|_{L^{m/p}}^{m/p}\le F_{\xi}(0)e^{-\omega t}.
 $$
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{d4:lem:transfer}
Assume $\delta_1(x)\equiv0$ and $\|G(t)\|_k\le C_Ge^{-\beta t}$ with $\beta>0$ and $k>\max\{1,N/2\}$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:alpha-b}
\tilde{\alpha}=\min\{a_1,\beta\},\qquad \tilde{b}=\begin{cases}1,&\beta=a_1,\\0,&\beta\ne a_1.\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then there is a constant $C_u$  such that
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:u-profile}
\|u(t)\|_\infty\le C_u(1+t)^{\tilde{b}} e^{-\tilde{\alpha} t}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{d4:thm:zero}
Under the assumptions of (\ref{zijia1}), $\delta_1(x)=\delta_2(x)\equiv 0$, $u_0(x), v_0(x)>0$ for every $x\in \Omega$, and $\frac{\partial u_0}{\partial \nu}=\frac{\partial v_0}{\partial \nu}$.
Moreover, either \eqref{eq:closed-weights} or \eqref{d4:eq:mu}. Let $C_G,\beta>0$ be those in \eqref{eq:forcing-table} and $\tilde{\alpha},\tilde{b},C_u$ be defined in Lemma~\ref{d4:lem:transfer}, and 
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:AB}
\tilde{A}=(s+1)a_2,\qquad \tilde{B}=r\tilde{\alpha},\qquad \rho=\tilde{b}r.
\end{equation}
Then 
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:v-envelope}
\|v(t)\|_\infty^{s+1}
\le\|v_0\|_\infty^{s+1}e^{-\tilde{A}t}
 +(s+1)C_u^r\mathcal{J}_{\tilde{A},\tilde{B},\rho}(t).
\end{equation}
In particular,  there is a constant $C_v$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:v-profile}
\|v(t)\|_\infty\le C_v(1+t)^\ell e^{-\tilde{a} t},\quad
\ell=\begin{cases}
 \tilde{b}r/(s+1),&\tilde{B}<\tilde{A},\\
 (\tilde{b}r+1)/(s+1),&\tilde{B}=\tilde{A},\\
 0,&\tilde{B}>\tilde{A},
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
and $\tilde{a}=\min\{a_2,r\tilde{\alpha}/(s+1)\}$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{d4:cor:loss}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{d4:thm:zero}, for any
$$
0<\gamma_u<\min\{a_1,\beta\},\qquad
0<\gamma_v<\min\{a_2,r\gamma_u/(s+1)\},
$$
there are constants $C_1,C_2$ such that
$\|u(t)\|_\infty\le C_1e^{-\gamma_ut}$ and
$\|v(t)\|_\infty\le C_2e^{-\gamma_vt}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{d4:thm:source}
Suppose that $\delta_1\equiv 0$, $\delta_2\not\equiv0$, and \eqref{eq:closed-weights}, \eqref{d4:eq:source-margin} hold. Then there exist constants $C_*,C_w>0$, depending on the data, fixed coefficients, source and selected weight, such that
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:sharp-u}
(\min u_0)e^{-a_1t}\le u(x,t)\le C_*e^{-a_1t},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:source-G-infty}
\|G(t)\|_\infty\le\eta_v^{-q}C_*^p e^{-pa_1t},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{d4:eq:w-profile}
\|v(t)-h_2\|_\infty\le
\begin{cases}
 C_we^{-\min\{a_2,ra_1\}t},&a_2\ne ra_1,\\
 C_w(1+t)e^{-a_2t},&a_2=ra_1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
In particular, $u\rightarrow 0$ and $v\rightarrow h_2$ uniformly.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
